title: seller-sku-bundle-playbook-and-legal-questions-wip
body:
Purpose: quick working playbook for SKU bundling options for cloud marketplace listings and a short legal/commercial question set to surface early with partners and legal. This is informal — notes + copy snippets + hooks for legal/product/cookbook.

Audience: Marketplace product manager, partner manager, solutions engineer, legal review (early).

Context (why we need this):
- Marketplace listings often require concrete SKU/plan definitions, SKU-level prices, trial/consumption rules, and language for support SLAs.
- Bundling strategy affects contract terms, revenue recognition, and customer expectations (esp. when combined with Dedicated or Private offerings).
- Team goal: produce a minimal, reviewable bundle definition and a short set of legal/commercial Qs to avoid rework during publisher certification.

High-level options (pick one for initial certification):
1) Consumption-only single SKU (hosted API): pay-per-token, free trial credits via marketplace voucher.
   - Pros: simplest compliance, minimal billing mapping.
   - Cons: harder to guarantee predictable spend for enterprise customers.
2) Flat monthly reserved SKU + overage (dedicated-lite): monthly commit (e.g., $X/month) maps to Dedicated burst credits; marketplace provides subscription SKU.
   - Pros: predictable revenue, easier to advertise SLOs for committed customers.
   - Cons: needs contract-level SLA alignment.
3) Hybrid bundle (base subscription + usage add-on): base listing shows feature tiers (Starter / Pro / Enterprise) with optional usage meter.
   - Pros: flexible; matches typical enterprise buying patterns.
   - Cons: more complex pricing copy and marketplace acceptance tests.

Checklist: Marketplace functional requirements (quick pass):
- [ ] SKU IDs (internal + marketplace) defined and mapped to internal product codes.
- [ ] Short marketing name (<= 50 chars) for each SKU.
- [ ] Short SKU description (<= 200 chars) that fits marketplace UI.
- [ ] Pricing model defined (per-token, per-embedding, per-seat, monthly fixed).
- [ ] Trial mechanics and voucher handling explained (how credits are consumed, expiry).
- [ ] Support channel and SLA summary (email, chat, enterprise phone) — include escalation path.
- [ ] Data residency / data handling blurb (for each SKU where applicable).
- [ ] Cancellation/refund policy mapped to marketplace rules.
- [ ] Legal contact and indemnity/liability high-level flags for legal to review.
- [ ] Billing reconciliation plan (how marketplace invoices feed to revenue ops).

Minimal required copy snippets (marketplace-ready, terse):
- Listing headline (single-line): "Redwood Inference — production-grade LLM inference: low-latency, cost-aware serving"
- Short blurb (1 sentence): "Run large language models with predictable latency and cost—hosted API, reserved capacity, or private deployments with observability and rollout controls."
- Feature bullets (3–5 max):
  - "Hosted API with streaming, tool-calling, and structured output"
  - "Reserved Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput and SLAs"
  - "Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) with KMS integration"
  - "Smart routing, caching, and batching to lower unit cost"
- Call-to-action: "Start with free credits — test against your latency budget"

Longer description (300–450 chars, optional extended copy):
"Redwood Inference delivers a unified runtime for serving LLMs in production. Choose hosted, reserved, or private modes to align with performance, security, and cost needs. Instrumented rollouts, token-level observability, and automated fallbacks keep applications reliable while lowering inference unit economics."

Suggested visuals (for marketplace asset upload):
- 1x hero screenshot: Console route-level latency dashboard (annotated)
- 1x diagram: Deployment modes (hosted / dedicated / private) with data flow
- 1x table: performance comparison (p95 latency, cost per 1M tokens) for curated models

Operational requirements matrix (to review with ops/finance):
- Commercial: subscription SKU mapping -> finance owner: @Lina Chen
- Billing cadence: monthly (marketplace invoiced) -> revops ticket reference: JIRA-PRJ-789
- Refund policy: follow marketplace default 30-day pro-rata? -> legal overlay required

Early legal/commercial questions (to surface in kickoff call with partner/legal):
1) Does the marketplace require a publisher master agreement or will marketplace terms govern customer relationship?
2) For Reserved SKUs, do we need to expose SLAs in listing copy or attach a separately-negotiated SLA for customers who opt-in?
3) Data residency: if the customer buys via marketplace in region X, does marketplace force data to remain in region X or can we route to nearest Redwood region?
4) Billing & refunds: marketplace handles customer invoices — how does chargeback work internally for committed Dedicated seats?
5) Liability caps and indemnities: is there an explicit conflict with existing Redwood terms? flag any mandatory marketplace clauses.
6) Export controls / restricted customer list: does marketplace block certain customers — how to reconcile with our sales pipeline?
7) Marketplace metadata requirements: taxonomy tags, support hours, security attestation checklist needed for listing.

Acceptance tests & publisher QA (quick runbook):
- Upload assets + copy into marketplace staging -> verify truncation and UI rendering of headline/description.
- Create a test purchase (trial voucher) -> verify billing flows to sandbox account and credit decrements.
- Validate SKU mapping to internal provisioning (API key created / allocation applied).
- Run smoke inference in marketplace-provisioned tenant -> measure p95 latency and cost per token against threshold.

Partner outreach snippets (short):
- Email subject: "Marketplace SKU mapping + short checklist — Redwood Inference"
- Body (short): "Hi <Partner_PM>, attaching our initial SKU bundling playbook and a couple of legal/commercial questions we want to confirm before publisher submission. TL;DR: prefer consumption-only SKU for first pass, hybrid bundle for next iteration. Can we sync Thurs 10–11 PT? — Asha"

Internal playbook: who does what (first-pass):
- GTM (Asha) : final copy, hero asset selection, partner comms
- Product (Marco) : pricing model, SKU code mapping, acceptance test signoff
- Legal (Evan) : answer Q1–Q7 above, draft any required addendum language
- Finance/RevOps (Lina) : billing mapping, revenue recognition notes
- Solutions Eng (SE assigned) : run provisioning smoke tests and latency checks

Open decisions (needs meeting):
- [ ] Default to consumption SKU or reserved SKU for first marketplace listing?
- [ ] If reserved, what is the minimum commit that is realistic for marketplace customers?
- [ ] Do we expose a simplified SLA in public listing or keep SLA in contract addendum?

Next steps (short-term):
1) Align on approach (consumption vs reserved) — target decision meeting 2024-09-18.
2) Draft final marketplace copy and attach assets — due 2024-09-25.
3) Legal kickoff to resolve Q1–Q7 — Evan to propose changes by 2024-10-02.
4) Upload to staging and run acceptance tests — SE to run by 2024-10-07.

Notes / brainstorming fragments (raw):
- Consider a small, labeled "trial pack" SKU that includes 1M tokens for $X — easier conversion than pure credit voucher.
- Could offer a burstable add-on for Dedicated that is billed as consumption above commit to satisfy spikes.
- Marketplace often strips HTML — avoid embedded links in the short description (use plain text).
- Need a short security boilerplate: "SOC2 Type II in progress / available on request" — confirm with security team.

Document history: draft started by Asha; collected inputs from Marco and Lina. Use this as the canonical early-playbook when talking to marketplace PMs.

Attachments: TBD (hero screenshots, compact pricing table CSV).

End of doc.
